1	# Style Guide
2	
3	This document outlines the coding standards and best practices for contributing to Discourse Graphs.
4	
5	## TypeScript Guidelines
6	
7	- Prefer `type` over `interface`
8	- Use explicit return types for functions
9	- Avoid `any` types when possible
10	- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
11	- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters
12	
13	## UI Guidelines
14	
15	- Use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling where possible
16	- When refactoring inline styles, use Tailwind classes.
17	- Use platform-native UI components first ([blueprintjs for Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/5BB8h4I7b), [Lucide icons for Obsidian](https://help.obsidian.md/Contributing+to+Obsidian/Style+guide), etc), with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) as a fallback
18	- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
19	- Follow responsive design principles
20	- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.
21	
22	## Code Formatting
23	
24	- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
25	- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
26	  - PascalCase for components and types
27	  - camelCase for variables and functions
28	  - UPPERCASE for constants
29	
30	## Code comments
31	
32	Ask: **What would a maintainer get wrong if this comment were removed?** If there is no specific answer, remove it.
33	
34	Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.
35	
36	Before keeping a comment, check:
37	
38	- **Necessary:** Would removing it hide information needed to safely change or use the code?
39	- **Accurate:** Does it match what the code actually does, including relevant limitations and exceptions?
40	- **Concise:** Can it be shortened without losing necessary information?
41	- **Durable:** Will it still matter after this PR merges?
42	- **Local:** Is it next to the code that depends on the information?
43	
44	Prefer one or two short sentences. Use longer explanations or examples when the constraint requires them; this is not a hard length limit.
45	
46	Do not restate function names, types, test names, assertions, or obvious operations. Do not repeat an explanation already documented at its source; link to it when needed.
47	
48	Put implementation history, review iterations, scope justifications, and ticket splits in inline GitHub comments. Keep durable constraints and known limitations in code or linked documentation. Link to the decision when describing behavior as agreed or accepted.
49	
50	Agents must check added and modified comments against these criteria before handoff. Authors must review them manually before requesting review.
51	
52	## Code Organization
53	
54	- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
55	- Co-locate code with its primary usage. Export it only for a concrete reuse need.
56	- Move code to `/utils` when it is shared across multiple call sites. Consider a shared package only after the code has stabilized and proven broadly reusable.
57	- Ground code movement in a current use case. Moving code because it feels cleaner adds churn without a clear functional benefit.
58	- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
59	- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
60	- Function names should describe their purpose clearly:
61	
62	```typescript
63	// ❌ Unclear and inline
64	const result = items.filter(
65	  (x) => x.date > now && x.status === "active" && !x.isArchived,
66	);
67	
68	// ✅ Clear and reusable
69	const getActiveUnarchivedItems = (items: Item[]) => {
70	  return items.filter(isActiveAndUnarchived);
71	};
72	
73	const isActiveAndUnarchived = (item: Item) => {
74	  return item.date > now && item.status === "active" && !item.isArchived;
75	};
76	```
77	
78	- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary:
79	
80	```typescript
81	  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
82	  // Check if user can access premium features
83	  const check = (user: User) => { ... }
84	
85	  // ✅ Self-documenting function name
86	  const hasValidPremiumSubscription = (user: User) => { ... }
87	```
88	
89	- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions:
90	
91	```typescript
92	// ❌ Large, multi-purpose function
93	const processData = (data: Data) => {
94	  // 30 lines of validation
95	  // 20 lines of transformation
96	  // 15 lines of formatting
97	};
98	
99	// ✅ Composed of focused functions
100	const processData = (data: Data) => {
101	  const validatedData = validateDataFormat(data);
102	  const transformedData = transformToDesiredFormat(validatedData);
103	  return formatForDisplay(transformedData);
104	};
105	```
106	
107	## Documentation
108	
109	- Use sentence case by default in docs and UI copy. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or page titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.
110	
111	## Code hygiene
112	
113	- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
114	- Handle errors gracefully and log enough context to diagnose failures without exposing credentials or sensitive data.
115	
116	## Testing
117	
118	- Write unit tests for new functionality
119	- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
120	- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
121	- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.
122

1	# PR guidelines
2	
3	This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.
4	
5	## Scope and structure
6	
7	- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
8	- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
9	- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
10	- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.
11	
12	## Size and review guidance
13	
14	About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.
15	
16	Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.
17	
18	Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.
19	
20	## Branches and PR metadata
21	
22	- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
23	- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
24	- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).
25	
26	## Before requesting review
27	
28	- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
29	- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
30	- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
31	- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
32	- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
33	- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
34	- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
35	- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.
36	
37	## After merge
38	
39	Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.
40

1	---
2	name: dg-pr-adherence-check
3	description: Review a PR or local diff for adherence to Discourse Graphs code standards and PR requirements, report concerns to the author, and return a Standards check checkbox. Use before handoff or requesting review, alongside scope-check.
4	---
5	
6	# PR adherence check
7	
8	Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.
9	
10	## Resolve the evidence
11	
12	1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
13	2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
14	3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
15	4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.
16	
17	## Evaluate adherence
18	
19	- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
20	- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
21	- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
22	- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
23	- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
24	- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.
25	
26	## Return the result
27	
28	Return a copy-ready section:
29	
30	```markdown
31	## Standards check
32	
33	- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
34	```
35	
36	The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.
37

1	---
2	name: scope-check
3	description: Compare a pull request or Git diff with a Linear engineering ticket's Done When criteria and produce a copy-ready PR scope check. Use when preparing or reviewing a PR, checking whether an implementation introduced broader abstractions or unsupported cases, or documenting why added scope is required now.
4	---
5	
6	# Scope Check
7	
8	Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.
9	
10	## Gather the Inputs
11	
12	1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
13	2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
14	3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
15	4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.
16	
17	## Evaluate Scope
18	
19	Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.
20	
21	- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
22	- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
23	- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.
24	
25	For each scope expansion, determine:
26	
27	1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
28	2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
29	3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?
30	
31	Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.
32	
33	## Format the Result
34	
35	Use this form when the diff stays within scope:
36	
37	```markdown
38	## Scope check
39	
40	- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
41	- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
42	```
43	
44	Use this form when the diff expands scope:
45	
46	```markdown
47	## Scope check
48	
49	- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
50	- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
51	- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
52	- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
53	- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
54	```
55	
56	If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.
57	
58	Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.
59

74	  return item.date > now && item.status === "active" && !item.isArchived;
75	};
76	```
77	
78	- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary:
79	
80	```typescript
81	  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
82	  // Check if user can access premium features
83	  const check = (user: User) => { ... }
84	
85	  // ✅ Self-documenting function name
86	  const hasValidPremiumSubscription = (user: User) => { ... }
87	```
88	
89	- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions:
90	
91	```typescript
92	// ❌ Large, multi-purpose function
93	const processData = (data: Data) => {
94	  // 30 lines of validation
95	  // 20 lines of transformation
96	  // 15 lines of formatting
97	};
98	
99	// ✅ Composed of focused functions
100	const processData = (data: Data) => {
101	  const validatedData = validateDataFormat(data);
102	  const transformedData = transformToDesiredFormat(validatedData);
103	  return formatForDisplay(transformedData);
104	};
105	```
106	
107	## Documentation
108	
109	- Use sentence case by default in docs and UI copy. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or page titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.
110	
111	## Code hygiene
112	
113	- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
114	- Handle errors gracefully and log enough context to diagnose failures without exposing credentials or sensitive data.
115	
116	## Testing
117	
118	- Write unit tests for new functionality
119	- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
120	- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
121	- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.
122

# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.

---
name: scope-check
description: Compare a pull request or Git diff with a Linear engineering ticket's Done When criteria and produce a copy-ready PR scope check. Use when preparing or reviewing a PR, checking whether an implementation introduced broader abstractions or unsupported cases, or documenting why added scope is required now.
---

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

1	---
2	name: pre-pr-review
3	description: Verification-first pre-PR review — mechanical checks against the diff, context docs, and schema, ending with a predicted-review simulation
4	user_invocable: true
5	---
6	
7	<skill-prompt>
8	Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).
9	
10	Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
11	- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
12	- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)
13	
14	## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)
15	
16	Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
17	- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
18	- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.
19	- A full pass on a follow-up push can still be the right call when there's genuine reason — the delta added surface beyond the feedback (the escape hatch below), the base moved under the branch, prior coverage looks doubtful or stale, or enough rounds have accumulated that the whole PR deserves fresh eyes. If you judge that, run full and say why.
20	- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.
21	
22	## Step 0 — Inventory
23	
24	The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
25	- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
26	- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
27	- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config
28	
29	Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.
30	
31	## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)
32	
33	If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:
34	
35	- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.
36	- **Findings closure first.** For every finding from the previous run and every reviewer/bot comment since: re-run the SPECIFIC check that produced it and report fixed / not-fixed / deferred+ticket per item. A fix claimed without re-verification is a failed step; a UI fix additionally gets re-driven (existing rule).
37	- Run steps 1–3 mechanically on the delta only, with Step 0's DATA/FRONTEND scoping applied to the delta. Step 4 shrinks to: every new hunk maps to the review feedback or the ticket, and the bot-comment gate on comments the new push attracted.
38	- Skip re-reading the context docs unless the delta touches DATA/FRONTEND files and they aren't already in context.
39	- Escape hatch: if the "follow-up" adds new surface (rebase onto a moved base, new feature code, a refactor beyond what was asked), it is not a re-review — run the full sequence on the full PR diff.
40	
41	## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)
42	
43	1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.
44	
45	1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.
46	
47	1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.
48	
49	1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).
50	
51	1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.
52	
53	1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
54	- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
55	- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
56	- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
57	- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
58	Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.
59	
60	1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). 1	You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
2	
3	## Dependencies
4	
5	Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.
6	
7	## Obsidian Style Guide
8	
9	Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.
10	
11	### Icons
12	
13	Platform-native UI.
14	Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.
15	
16	Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.
17	
18	Guidelines for icons
19	
20	Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
21	Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
22	Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
23	Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.
24	
25	Use the SVG version of the icons available.

You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands
- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;
  if (view instanceof MyCustomView) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

- Do not detach leaves during plugin unload

### Editor

- Prefer the Editor API over `Vault.modify()` when the note is currently open in the editor
- Prefer `Vault.process()` instead of `Vault.modify()` to modify a file in the background

### Mobile compatibility

- Node.js and Electron APIs (`fs`, `crypto`, `os`) are unavailable on mobile
- If the plugin targets mobile, use web API equivalents: `SubtleCrypto` instead of `crypto`, `navigator.clipboard` for clipboard access
- Regex lookbehind assertions are not supported on some mobile — avoid them if possible
- The plugin ships with `isDesktopOnly: false`, so it must load on mobile
- Node builtins and `electron` are deliberately not in the esbuild `external` array in `scripts/compile.ts`. Marking them external lets a dependency's `require("fs")` reach the bundle and throw on mobile; leaving them out fails the build instead. Replace the dependency rather than re-adding the external

### Code quality

- Use `const`/`let` — never `var`
- Prefer `async`/`await` over `.then()` chains
- Minimize `console.log` — remove debug logs before shipping
- Do not hardcode styles inline — use CSS classes and Obsidian's CSS variables

## Unit tests

Vitest runs the plugin's pure logic in a Node environment: `pnpm test:unit` (or `pnpm test:watch` while working). The repository-wide `pnpm ci:validate` picks it up through the `test:unit` script.

- Put tests in `src/**/__tests__/<module>.test.ts`, next to the code they cover. Tests covering the test scaffolding itself live in `test/`; those two globs are the whole of `include` in `vitest.config.mts`.
- Import the module under test through the `~` alias, as the source does.
- `obsidian` ships type declarations with no runtime entry point, so `vitest.config.mts` aliases it to `test/obsidianStub.ts`. Add to that stub whatever a new test needs to load its module; use `vi.mock("obsidian")` in the test itself when the test needs to assert on a call.
- Obsidian's own objects are large. Build the slice the code path reads and cast it (`{ metadataCache: … } as unknown as App`) rather than constructing a whole `App` or `TFile`.
- Logic that needs a live vault, editor, or workspace is not covered here — extract the decision into a util and test that.

### Keeping the stub honest

The stub is hand-written, so it can be wrong about the API today and can fall behind when the `obsidian` dependency is bumped. Two mechanisms catch that. Each runs under exactly one command, so run `pnpm ci:validate` to get both.

`test/obsidianStub.conformance.ts` type-checks each stub member against the real declaration. It is type-only and matches none of the vitest globs, so only `pnpm check-types` enforces it. Keep it inside the `tsconfig.json` include, or the drift check disappears with no signal.

- Members with real behavior are fully conformant.
- Shells, which exist only so an importing module loads, are checked for the export name alone. When a shell gains behavior, move it to the conformant group.
- Every export must appear in one group or the other, so adding one without classifying it fails the build.

`test/obsidianStub.test.ts` pins the behavior the stub reimplements, which the type checker cannot see. It is type-checked like any other file, but only `pnpm test:unit` runs its assertions.

### Verifying the stub

Type declarations cannot tell you what a function returns for a given input, so do not guess it. Obsidian ships its implementation in `obsidian.asar`, in the resources directory of the installed app, and the current cases were settled by reading it. Two details it settled: `normalizePath("/")` returns `"/"`, and `TFolder.isRoot()` tests `path === "/"` rather than a null parent.

The bundle is minified, so it takes two steps: find the exported name to learn its minified name, then find that function. The example below is a macOS path; on Windows and Linux locate `obsidian.asar` under the install directory and substitute it.

```
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/Resources/obsidian.asar","utf8");
  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: pre-pr-review
3	description: Verification-first pre-PR review — mechanical checks against the diff, context docs, and schema, ending with a predicted-review simulation
4	user_invocable: true
5	---
6	
7	<skill-prompt>
8	Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).
9	
10	Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
11	- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
12	- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)
13	
14	## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)
15	
16	Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
17	- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
18	- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.
19	- A full pass on a follow-up push can still be the right call when there's genuine reason — the delta added surface beyond the feedback (the escape hatch below), the base moved under the branch, prior coverage looks doubtful or stale, or enough rounds have accumulated that the whole PR deserves fresh eyes. If you judge that, run full and say why.
20	- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.
21	
22	## Step 0 — Inventory
23	
24	The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
25	- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
26	- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
27	- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config
28	
29	Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.
30	
31	## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)
32	
33	If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:
34	
35	- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.
36	- **Findings closure first.** For every finding from the previous run and every reviewer/bot comment since: re-run the SPECIFIC check that produced it and report fixed / not-fixed / deferred+ticket per item. A fix claimed without re-verification is a failed step; a UI fix additionally gets re-driven (existing rule).
37	- Run steps 1–3 mechanically on the delta only, with Step 0's DATA/FRONTEND scoping applied to the delta. Step 4 shrinks to: every new hunk maps to the review feedback or the ticket, and the bot-comment gate on comments the new push attracted.
38	- Skip re-reading the context docs unless the delta touches DATA/FRONTEND files and they aren't already in context.
39	- Escape hatch: if the "follow-up" adds new surface (rebase onto a moved base, new feature code, a refactor beyond what was asked), it is not a re-review — run the full sequence on the full PR diff.
40	
41	## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)
42	
43	1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.
44	
45	1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.
46	
47	1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.
48	
49	1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).
50	
51	1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.
52	
53	1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
54	- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
55	- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
56	- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
57	- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
58	Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.
59	
60	1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.
61	
62	1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)
63	
64	1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).
65	
66	## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)
67	
68	2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.
69	
70	2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).
71	
72	2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?
73	
74	2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.
75	
76	2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."
77	
78	2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).
79	
80	## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)
81	
82	Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
83	- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
84	- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
85	- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
86	- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
87	- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
88	- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
89	- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
90	- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
91	- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)
92	- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)
93	
94	## Step 4 — Process gate
95	
96	- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
97	- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

**Setup is done**
- origin/main is still 67e93a0d. On it, I confirmed all three problems still exist and the tickets share no files.
- I created the three worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/eng-220{9,8,7}` on the Linear branch names, and assigned ENG-2208 and ENG-2207 to you.
- **All three worktrees got a frozen install, not just ENG-2209.** The main checkout is at 98b36b55, behind origin/main in `packages/database` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Symlinked node_modules would have resolved `@repo/database` to that stale copy. Each install took about 4s.
- **`core.hooksPath` was already the relative `.husky/_` before I installed anything**, probably left by an earlier session's install. It's now set back to `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.husky/_`.
- The ENG-2209 and ENG-2208 implementers are running. ENG-2207 starts when one of them finishes.

**ENG-2207 description update (draft, needs your approval before I save it)**

Only Problem, Solution, Done When and Out of Scope change. Notes stays as it is.

> ## Problem
>
> * Node type schemas can store `format` at `literal_content.format` or the legacy `literal_content.source_data.format`.
> * The shared resolver exists: `resolveSchemaFormat` (`packages/utils/src/resolveSchemaFormat.ts`) landed with ENG-2156 in PR #1331, and Roam's import reads the format through it.
> * Obsidian's import doesn't. `parseSchemaLiteralContent` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`) reads `source_data.format` first. When a schema has both keys, Obsidian imports the legacy value and Roam imports the top-level value.
>
> ## Solution
>
> * Read the format in `parseSchemaLiteralContent` through `resolveSchemaFormat`.
> * Leave the `color`, `tag` and `keyImage` reads unchanged.
>
> ## Done When
>
> * Obsidian import tests cover the top-level value, legacy fallback, conflicting values, and missing values.
> * Roam and Obsidian use the shared resolver, and the top-level value wins when both exist.
>
> ## Out of Scope
>
> * Changing schema writers, migrating existing rows, or removing the legacy fallback.
> * Client-version enforcement or a general metadata migration framework.
> * A test runner for `packages/utils`. The cases run in Obsidian's vitest suite through the import path.

**One question:** the title still says "Add shared node type format resolver to `@repo/utils`", and the PR title has to match it exactly. I'd keep the title and let the updated description explain. The alternative is renaming it to "Read Obsidian node type format through the shared resolver".

I'll continue with the diffs when the implementers report back.

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Reviewer brief

- **Result:** When an imported node type's template has no title, Obsidian now creates a template file named `<node type name> (from <source space name>)` and assigns it to the new node type. Templates with an explicit title take the same path as before. With the Templates plugin off or no templates folder set, a Roam node type with a template now shows the existing "imported without template" notice, as Obsidian node types already did.
- **Review focus:**
  - Diagnosis (the ticket asks to confirm it): Roam never writes a template title. Sync (`discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept`) writes `literal_content` as `{ label, format, template_content, roles }`, and ENG-2202's test pins that shape ("writes the template body to template_content, with no template title"). Publish sets `CrossAppNodeSchema.template` but never `templateTitle`, so `crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept` writes no `literal_content.template` either. `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` created a template only when both fields were present, so it skipped every Roam template. ENG-2202 merged on 2026-09-28 but isn't in a Roam release yet; the released extension (0.22.0) still writes the body to `literal_content.template`. Until the next Roam release, this PR imports templates only from rows written by builds from main that include ENG-2202. On the first sync after that release, ENG-2175's format backfill rewrites rows from released extensions in the new shape, because they have no `format`. Rows last written by builds from main between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-28 have `format` and keep the old shape.
  - Fallback filename: the name carries the source space, using the existing `getImportedTemplateFileName` convention (`Evidence (from my-graph)`). The create path assigns a file that already exists at the requested name ("local file takes precedence"), so a bare node type name would assign an unrelated local `Evidence.md`. With the suffix, an existing file at the fallback name is an earlier import from a space with the same name, and a repeated import reuses it instead of creating a duplicate.
  - Valid filename: `sanitizeFileName` removes `* " \ / < > : | ?`. Obsidian's `vault.create` rejects `:` on every platform and the rest on Windows, and `* ? < > "` on Android too (checked in the 1.13.7 app bundle). The name always ends in `)`, which also rules out Windows' trailing dot or space and its reserved names. A name with no valid characters becomes `Imported template (from <space>)`. The fallback name stays within 200 UTF-8 bytes: a long node type name is cut at a code point boundary, and if the ` (from <space>)` suffix alone doesn't fit, the node type imports without a template and shows a notice.
  - `sourceSpaceName` comes from the space info `importNodes` already fetches, threaded through `importRelationsForImportedNodes`, the other caller of `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal`.
- **Risk or follow-up:**
  - Not yet exercised in Obsidian against a live Roam import.
  - Legacy Roam rows (see the diagnosis): on main and with this PR, the body is stored as the node type's template reference, so node creation warns that it cannot apply the template. A node type already imported from such a row keeps that reference after a backfill, because updating templates on existing local node types is out of scope here.
  - The node type settings panel's template import (`templateImport.ts`) still requires a title, so it skips Roam templates. That path imports into existing node types, which this ticket leaves out of scope; follow-up ticket to be filed.
  - Two node types from one space whose names differ only by removed characters (`Question?` and `Question`), or only after the point where a long name is cut to fit 200 bytes, derive the same fallback filename, so the second is assigned the first one's template file.

## Verification

On `1830b19a`:

- `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on the changed files: 0 errors. `importRelations.ts` and the test are clean. `importNodes.ts` reports 5 warnings, all on lines this diff does not touch; `origin/main` has the same 5.
- `npx prettier --check` on the changed files: pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck` (apps/obsidian): pass.
- `pnpm test:unit` (apps/obsidian): 8 files, 93 tests pass. Without the fallback name, the 3 untitled-template tests fail; without the length bound, the 5 length tests fail.
- `pnpm ci:validate`: pass.
- `npx turbo run build --filter=@discourse-graphs/obsidian`: pass.

Pending.

- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.

Every caller of the old per-app builders reads titles through one builder in `@repo/database/lib`, and every `{content}` extraction, including the Discourse context "Content:" line, goes through one extractor there; `sourceIdOfNode` keeps its `{source}` lookup (parity table). The one exception is Roam's export (`exportUtils.getContentFromNodes`), which keeps its own builder and extractor (see Risk or follow-up). Formats without those characters build the same regex as before (pinned in the builder tests).

  - Parity with the replaced copies:

    | Old | New | Parity |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Obsidian `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` | `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` in `@repo/database/lib/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` | changed: literal text also escapes `( ) * ^ $ \| { } \`. Same regex for formats without them. |
    | Roam `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` (default export) and `getDiscourseNodeFormatInnerExpression` | same names, named exports of that module | changed: same escaping change |
    | Obsidian `extractContentFromTitle(format, title)` | `extractContentFromTitle(format, title)` in `@repo/database/lib/extractContentFromTitle` | changed: a format with placeholders but no `{content}` returns the title instead of the first capture, as Roam and `decorateTitle` already did. Nothing reads `BulkImportCandidate.extractedContent`, so the observable Obsidian change is the published `core_title` and the Content line for imported node types without `{content}`. Obsidian's settings refuse to save such a format. |

    | Roam `extractFieldFromTitle(title, node, "source")` | inline `{source}` lookup in `sourceIdOfNode` | changed: same grammar change, and `sourceIdOfNode` now uses the cached `matcherFor` regex instead of compiling one per call. Kept in `sourceSlot.ts` rather than the package because the source slot hack is temporary. |
    | `DiscourseContextView` inline `extractContentFromTitle` | the shared `extractContentFromTitle` | changed: renders the trimmed `{content}` capture instead of the first capture, and the whole basename for a format without `{content}`, which is what `discourseNodeInstanceToLocalConcept` publishes |

  - Roam placeholder grammar: the old scan counted tokens such as `{x1}` (digits, `_`, `-`) that the builder never captured, which shifted every later capture index. Only titles that literally contain such a token extract differently, and they now get the right capture.
  - Datalog: `discourseNodeFormatToDatalog` (through `regexRePatternValue`), `escapeRegexPatternForDatalog`, and `getAllDiscourseNodesSince` double backslashes before putting the regex source in an EDN string, so the new escapes reach `re-pattern` intact. `discourseNodeFormatToDatalog.test.ts` covers the first path. Obsidian `formatNodeName` parses the regex source and strips every backslash, so its output does not change.
- Risk or follow-up:
  - Not yet exercised in Roam or Obsidian.
  - `core_title` rows already written with the fallback value are not repaired (out of scope).
  - Roam specifications store the regex the builder produced when they were enabled. One generated earlier from a format with `( ) * ^ $ | { } \` keeps its old regex, which can miss its own titles or match other pages, and `matchDiscourseNode` and `discourseNodeFormatToDatalog` read it instead of the format. Turning the specification off and on regenerates it. Turning it off deletes every condition, so this suits only a specification nobody edited; an edited one needs its `target` changed by hand. A value-aware rewrite of stored specifications is a follow-up ticket to be filed.
  - Export keeps its own builder and extractor (`exportUtils.getContentFromNodes`): it escapes metacharacters except braces, treats any `{...}` as a placeholder, matches `{content}` case-sensitively and falls back to the title on an empty capture. Swapping it for the shared one would change export file names for formats without metacharacters, so it moves with the fill-side placeholder scans (`formatUtils.ts` and `ModifyNodeDialog.tsx` fill `{[\w\d-]*}`; `Export.tsx` and `Tldraw.tsx` scan `{[\w\d-]+}`) to a follow-up ticket to be filed.
  - Draft #1412 (ENG-2143) imports the deleted Roam `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` module, and draft #710 imports the deleted Roam `extractContentFromTitle` module. Both will need updating on rebase.
  - No test renders the Discourse context view (apps/obsidian runs vitest without a DOM). The view calls the same function with the same inputs as the converter, and the converter is tested.

- `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` and `npx prettier --check` on the two changed test files: pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck` in `apps/roam` and `packages/database`: pass.
- `pnpm test:unit`: roam 608 and database 103 tests pass.
- `pnpm ci:validate`: pass.

On `42e6c4df`:

- `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <changed files>` in `apps/roam`, `apps/obsidian`, and `packages/database`: no errors. The 13 warnings reported in 6 changed app files are on untouched lines and appear identically on `065cab5e`.
- `npx prettier --check <changed files>` and `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck` in all three: pass.
- `npx turbo run build --filter=roam` and `npx turbo run build --filter=@discourse-graphs/obsidian`: built with 0 errors.

Two tooling gotchas that silently dropped outward actions on 2026-09-16.

- `gh pr edit <n> --body-file … / --add-reviewer …` exits 1 on DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph with "GraphQL: Projects (classic) is being deprecated … (repository.pullRequest.projectCards)" and applies nothing. Use the REST API instead: `gh api -X PATCH repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pulls/<n> -F body=@file` and `gh api -X POST repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pulls/<n>/requested_reviewers -f 'reviewers[]=<login>'`. `gh pr comment`, `gh pr merge`, `gh pr view` are unaffected.
